long_biography.plain_text:
Broadcasting was already a family enterprise when Theodore M. Kyriakou joined Antenna in 1996. His father, Minos, had moved a long-established shipping family into private Greek radio and television. Kyriakou developed that platform through acquisitions, restructuring and partnerships, extending it from a domestic broadcaster into an international media and entertainment group.

The strategy mixed owned operations with targeted investments. Antenna bought television networks in Southeast Europe, added streaming, cinema, radio and digital businesses, and backed technology and media companies through specialist investment partnerships. Kyriakou also became lead shareholder of the family's K Group, whose other holdings include shipping, property and asset management. He serves on the board of Raine, a merchant bank specialising in technology, media, telecommunications and sport.

Strong sources establish that Theodore entered a broadcaster founded and owned by his father, that the siblings control the family group after Minos Kyriakou's death, and that Theodore materially expanded Antenna.
